Subject: Module proof-pack and CI acceptance criteria for on-prem deployment

Hi John / Acme team,

Attached is the module proof-pack we discussed for the on-prem VPC deployment. This is intended to be the minimum set of artifacts your auditors asked for so your compliance team can sign off on the Terraform / Helm / Ansible modules and our CI/CD gating. The zip contains: signed terraform module tarballs, module_manifest.txt (git SHAs + checksums), helm-chart-archives, ansible-playbooks with lint outputs, and a short README that maps artifacts to acceptance criteria. I've also attached a screenshot from the pipeline run that produced the artifacts.

High-level ask: can your security/compliance team confirm whether the following acceptance criteria are sufficient, or if we need additional evidence? If acceptable, we propose a gated sign-off workflow and a short verification window (3 business days) before we proceed to environment provisioning.

Acceptance checklist (summary):
- Artifact provenance: git commit id, tag, and signed tarball with checksum
- Artifact signing: cosign/cosigned artifacts for container/helm; GPG-signed module bundles for TF
- Reproducible build proof: build logs and deterministic flags used in pipeline
- Pipeline evidence: CI run logs, artifact locations, pipeline SHA, and screenshots (see pipeline-run-20280330.png)
- SBOM for images used by Helm charts (CycloneDX or SPDX)
- KMS key id used to sign artifacts and KMS rotation policy reference
- Ansible playbook lint + idempotency run (summary tests)
- Promotion & rollback steps documented for staging -> prod promotion, and automated rollback hooks
- Network segmentation diagram for the private/VPC topology (egress, peering, bastion layout)

Attachments: acme-proofpack-20280330.zip, pipeline-run-20280330.png

Timeline: if we can get confirmation on scope today/tomorrow we will schedule the verification run for Tue/Wed (next week) and aim to have evidence posted to the shared drive by end of week.

Thanks — tagging Karthik and Kimberly for any missing internal items or additional compliance notes.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Delivery
Redwood Inference

Marissa — thanks for the packet. Quick clarifying questions from our side:
1) When you say "GPG-signed module bundles for TF" — do you publish the public keys and a signed attest? Our auditors prefer a signed provenance statement that we can independently verify.
2) Retention period: what retention window do you anticipate for the signed artifacts and logs? Our policy needs 7 years for certain audit trails (we can scope which artifacts).
3) Do you provide attestations or an attestor service endpoint for verifying cosign signatures, or do we need to run local verification?

If you can answer the three points and confirm the schedule, we'll route this to our compliance team for review.

—John

John — great questions. Summary answers and added checklist items below (pasted and expanded from Marissa's list):

- Public verification keys and attestations: we publish cosign public keys and a provenance attestation file for each signed image/chart in the proof-pack. The attestation includes the signing key ID, subject digest, and the builder metadata. We will add a top-level "attestations/" folder in the proof-pack with signatures and a short README explaining verification commands.
- Retention: Redwood stores signed artifacts and CI logs for a minimum of 2 years by default in the artifact storage for hosted evidence. For enterprise/private deployments we can extend that to 7 years under the enterprise evidence retention addendum — we'll need Procurement to capture that in the contract addendum.
- Attestor endpoint: we provide an optional attestations endpoint (read-only) for customers who request it; for Acme we can enable the endpoint and provide a signed TLS cert. Local verification is possible using cosign/gpg as well.

Additional technical items we recommend you verify as part of acceptance:
- SBOMs: CycloneDX JSON for every image referenced by Helm charts
- Signed Helm chart provenance with cosign and chart provenance files
- KMS binding: key id in proof-pack + KMS policy snippet; confirm whether you want Redwood-managed key or your HSM via customer-managed key (CMK) option
- Network diagram (attached in drive link) showing private Egress firewall rules + required endpoints for attestations; include CIDR ranges and port lists for minimal allowlist
- Git commit-to-release mapping: single file listing module repo URL, git commit, tag, and artifact SHA

I opened a quick Jira to track outstanding items: ACME-214 (proof-pack additional evidence) — link: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/ACME-214. I'll add the attestation README and SBOMs to the drive folder by EOD.

Neha Kapoor
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

John / team — adding CI/CD gating details so Acme's ops team knows how we validated the modules:

CI gate & validation summary:
- Source-to-artifact pipeline: GitLab CI (primary) -> build job produces deterministic artifact using pinned toolchain. Job records exact compiler/tool versions in build-metadata.json.
- Reproducible build check: we run two independent builders (builder-a, builder-b) and compare artifact checksums; mismatch goes to manual review.
- Signature step: artifacts are uploaded to artifact bucket and signed by Redwood's signing service using a CMK when customer-managed KMS is configured; otherwise Redwood-managed key with auditable KMS access logs.
- CI evidence collection: pipeline run logs, artifact checksums, cosign verification output, SBOMs, and the build-metadata.json are packaged into proof-pack zip.
- Promotion gates: automated smoke tests in a staging enclave; manual compliance approval step (UI + audit trail) then gated promotion to customer-provisioned environment.

Practical asks for Acme before we run the verification:
1) Provide the CIDR and firewall admin contact for the environment where the attestations endpoint will be allowed (we need to register the endpoint for read-only access).
2) Confirm whether you want Redwood to host the attestation endpoint under the enterprise addendum (we can provide TLS cert and ACLs), or if you will host a local attestations mirror.
3) If you require 7-year retention, Procurement to confirm and we'll update the artifact bucket lifecycle policy for this deal.

I've attached a one-page checklist (ci-gate-checklist.md) and I can run a demo of the verification steps next Tue. If Acme can provide the firewall CIDR and a primary contact by EOD Monday we can hold the verification window Tue-Wed.

Karthik Iyer
